statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail returns to 24% from 20% because the retracement that justified the previous reading failed: NQ December extended the Globex low to 30,409.25, below the 30,430.00 low that had held, and trades 30,424.75 at 03:16:17Z in the lower fifth of the overnight band. Stress firms to 78% with the ten-year at 5.24% and WTI at $93.94. Tail remains one point below the blocking threshold.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH for NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD, with Tail at 24% at the top of the watch band and one point below the blocking threshold. The step up is driven by an observed failed retracement, not by the calendar. The previous assessment scored 20% because price had retraced about 76 points off the 30,430.00 Globex low to 30,505.75, which it named as evidence that mean reversion was working. That retracement did not hold. The low was extended a fourth time, to 30,409.25, and NQ December reads 30,424.75 at 03:16:17Z on one publisher and 30,424.50 at 03:16:16Z on a second, with a 30,450.25 print at 03:18:48Z leaving price roughly 41 points above the low and about 20% up a 30,409.25 to 30,616.00 band. A failed retracement followed by a further low, with price held in the lower fifth of the range, is the pattern this contract treats as an amplifier, and it is now the fourth successive lower low of the overnight session. Three considerations hold the reading inside the watch band rather than the blocking band. The net move is only -0.38% against the 30,566.25 previous close, so the extension is shallow in absolute terms. The VIX closed at 16.07, up 8.07% but a low level, and options are not pricing the sustained no-retracement path a higher reading would require. The Nikkei 225 at 65,307.00 as of 02:35Z has recovered to -0.87% from an earlier -1.11% and sits about 248 points above its 65,058.86 low, so the regional tape conflicts with NQ rather than confirming it, and conflict belongs in Stress. Stress at 78% carries the unresolved backdrop: the ten-year at 5.24% after Monday's 5.274% high, the highest since June 2007, the thirty-year near 5.55%, WTI extending 1.45% to $93.94 and Brent to $106.81 after Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and Monday's violent single-name dispersion in semiconductors. The published danger window covers 13:30Z to 15:00Z, spanning the US cash open, the simultaneous JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence releases at 14:00Z, and the hour in which a delayed second leg would form.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures extend the Globex low to 30,409.25 after a failed 76-point retracement; Tail firms back to 24% with Stress at 78%
body: The 03:00Z clock-hour reverses the relief that defined the previous assessment. At 02:34Z the reading was cut from 24% to 20% on the specific ground that NQ December had retraced roughly 76 points off a 30,430.00 Globex low to 30,505.75, which the contract treats as mean reversion demonstrated on the same instrument in the same session. That retracement failed. The low was extended a fourth time, to 30,409.25, and the freshest verified prints are 30,424.75 at 03:16:17Z on Yahoo Finance and 30,424.50 at 03:16:16Z on Investing.com, both showing -0.46% against a 30,566.25 previous close, with a subsequent 30,450.25 print at 03:18:48Z reading -0.38%. Against a session band of 30,409.25 to 30,616.00 on one publisher and 30,409.25 to 30,605.25 on the other, price sits roughly 41 points above the low and about 20% up the range. The overnight sequence is now 30,536.25, 30,468.25, 30,430.00 and 30,409.25: four successive lower lows, with the single meaningful retracement of the night rejected. Under this contract that combination, repeated extension after a failed retracement with price held in the lower fifth of the band, is the amplifier being scored, so Tail returns to 24% and the dominant mode reverts to trend-down. What keeps the reading inside the watch band is the modest scale and the absence of confirmation. The whole overnight excursion spans about 207 points, roughly 0.68%, and the net change from the previous close is -0.38%, so the path is drifting rather than repricing violently. The VIX closed at 16.07, up 8.07% on the day within a 15.68 to 16.62 range, and that absolute level is not consistent with index options pricing the sustained denial of retracement a blocking reading would require. The regional tape actively conflicts: the Nikkei 225 read 65,307.00 at 02:35Z, down 0.87%, having recovered roughly 248 points off its 65,058.86 low inside a 65,058.86 to 65,805.08 range, so Japanese cash is repairing while NQ makes new lows. The contract is explicit that conflicting signals normally raise Stress rather than Tail, and that is where the unresolved conditions sit. Stress firms a point to 78%. The ten-year Treasury yield is 5.24%, up six basis points on Monday within a 5.20 to 5.27 range, after touching 5.274% intraday for the highest level since June 2007, with the thirty-year reported near 5.55% and the two-year at 4.81% on the latest 25 September H.15 observation. Crude has extended rather than stabilised: WTI is $93.94 and Brent $106.81, each up 1.45% on Tuesday, after President Trump rejected Iran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, telling Axios that Tehran had overplayed its hand while adding that talks are expected to resume this week. The strait remains effectively closed, and Iranian officials are reported to be pessimistic about a deal before the November midterms. That is a live, unscheduled headline channel rather than a calendar item, which is one reason the environment is difficult rather than pathological. Monday's equity internals were the widest in weeks. The Nasdaq-100 index closed at 30,276.81, down 1.08%, after trading as low as 30,081.06 within a 30,081.06 to 30,480.40 range, so cash recovered close to 196 points into its own close. Beneath that, verified reporting has Arm down about 9%, Qualcomm about 6% and Marvell about 5%, with the semiconductor ETF off 3% against a 1% decline in the Nasdaq-100 proxy, and JPMorgan separately flagging AI disruption risk across software, business services and media. Latest-session basket context, which is delayed and is not evidence of current NQ structure, shows seven of eight megacaps lower with a mean of -1.48% and a semiconductor set averaging -3.86% with 3.35 points of dispersion. The shared context file was read this hour but is not usable as fresh evidence: its collection status is partial, its futures and calendar sections are unavailable, and its 01:18:28Z collection time is roughly 147 minutes old, beyond the 90-minute freshness limit, so the full independent research above carries the assessment. Confidence holds at 88% because the price path is corroborated by two independent quotes within one second of each other plus a third a minute later, and the cash close, the volatility index, the long end, the H.15 observation, crude, the Asian tape, the seven-day calendar and the geopolitical development were each read from primary or reputable current sources during this hour. The day ahead is medium-weight before a heavy one. Case-Shiller and the FHFA House Price Index print at 13:00Z, the cash open follows at 13:30Z, JOLTS Job Openings and CB Consumer Confidence arrive together at 14:00Z, and Goolsbee, Musalem and Williams speak at 17:00Z, 17:30Z and 18:00Z. The larger checkpoints are Wednesday's ADP at 12:15Z and Core PCE with final second-quarter GDP at 12:30Z, Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter results after Wednesday's close, and Friday's payrolls report. None of those sits inside the current hour, and a scheduled event ahead is not counted here as structure already observed.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from the European pre-open of 28 September to the last hour before this assessment. The window opened at 21% Tail with Stress at 78% during the overnight long-end repricing, and stayed inside the 21-24% watch band through the European morning as yields extended. Two hours touched the elevated band and neither persisted: 09:00Z at 26% during the European yield move and 14:00Z at 27% around the US cash open, each back inside the watch band within a single hour. Stress peaked at 85% at 10:00Z before easing to 76-78% from the cash close onward, while Confidence improved steadily from 79% to 88% as the session produced verifiable price-path evidence. Tail then decayed to 17-19% across the five contained hours after the Globex reopen before jumping to 24% at 01:00Z when the three-hour overnight floor broke, and easing to 20% at 02:00Z on a retracement that has since failed. Dominant mode ran trend-down through the European morning, mixed across most of the US session and evening, and normal through the quiet reopen. Every one of the 24 slots is backed by a published Claude assessment; none is reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The conditional path opens at 24% for the current 03:00Z hour, where the failed retracement and the fourth successive lower low are the observed evidence. It eases to 23% for the Asian mid-morning test of 30,409.25 and to 22% across the Tokyo lunch, the Tokyo close and the European open on an assumption of restored two-way flow. Tail firms to 23% through the London morning and the 09:00Z hour that printed 26% a day earlier, then eases to 22% across the late European morning and the pre-US lull. The US block carries the peak: 23% for the 13:00Z window containing Case-Shiller and the cash open, 24% at 14:00Z where JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence print together and Stress reaches 82%, and 23% at 15:00Z for delayed second-leg risk as the danger window closes. It then decays to 22% through the US afternoon around the 17:00Z to 18:00Z Fed speakers, to 21% in the power hour, 20% at the cash close and 19% across the maintenance halt and the Globex reopen, where the mapped state returns to EA_ON on venue mechanics rather than on an improved backdrop. The final four slots run 20-21% for the late-evening and Tokyo-morning handover that broke the floor a day earlier, ahead of ADP, Core PCE and final Q2 GDP later on 30 September. Confidence decays from 88% to 77% with distance from the evidence cutoff. No slot is modelled at or above the 25% blocking threshold, and every hour after the current one frames its structure conditionally.

forecastDetail.comment: The opening hour of the forecast is the only one anchored in observed evidence. NQ December extended the Globex low to 30,409.25, taking out the 30,430.00 low that had held an hour earlier, after the 76-point retracement to 30,505.75 failed to hold. Two publishers agree on the level: 30,424.75 at 03:16:17Z on Yahoo Finance and 30,424.50 at 03:16:16Z on Investing.com, with a 30,450.25 print at 03:18:48Z leaving price roughly 41 points above the low and about 20% up the 30,409.25-30,616.00 band. That is repeated extension after a failed retracement with price in the lower fifth of the range, which is the specific evidence this contract treats as an amplifier, so Tail returns to 24% and the dominant mode reverts to trend-down. It stops one point short of the blocking band because the total move is only -0.38% from the 30,566.25 previous close, the VIX at 16.07 is not pricing a sustained no-retracement path, and the Nikkei is recovering rather than confirming.

The Asian mid-morning hour is a pure test of the 30,409.25 low. Tail eases one point to 23% on the assumption that the bounce above 30,450 broadens into two-way flow, which is the base case whenever the fourth successive low is met with a bid. The invalidation is specific and worth stating: a fifth lower low met with a retracement materially smaller than the 41 points already seen would establish the persistent directional efficiency this contract requires, and would move the assessment into the blocking band rather than within the watch band. Stress is unchanged at 78% because the ten-year at 5.24% and WTI at $93.94 do not move on an hourly timescale.

Tokyo lunch and the Asian afternoon are the thinnest window of the NQ day, and the modelled path reflects that rather than any new information: Tail 22%, Stress easing a point to 77%. Thin flow historically produces wider retracements, which is the condition under which the reverse and grid mechanism works, so the conditional reading improves even though nothing in the cross-asset backdrop has changed. The assumption behind this slot is that no fresh US-Iran headline lands inside it; Trump's rejection of Tehran's seven-day Strait of Hormuz proposal is already in the tape, but talks are expected to resume this week and the timing is not scheduled.

The Tokyo cash close at 06:00Z is the handover checkpoint for this slot. The Nikkei 225 read 65,307.00 at 02:35Z, down 0.87%, having recovered roughly 248 points from its 65,058.86 session low within a 65,058.86 to 65,805.08 range. If it closes nearer the high than the low, the divergence between a recovering Japanese cash market and an NQ contract making successive lower lows widens further, and under this contract conflicting cross-asset signals belong in Stress and Confidence rather than in Tail. Tail is therefore held at 22% and Stress at 77% for the handover.

European cash markets open inside this window. Monday's analogue matters: the 07:00Z to 10:00Z block produced the strongest pre-US Tail readings of that session, including a 26% print at 09:00Z as European yields extended. Tail is nevertheless held at 22% here rather than pre-positioned higher, because the contract is explicit that hypothetical future alignment must not be counted as already observed. Stress firms a point to 78% to reflect that a European open which re-prices the long end is a Stress event first. The working assumption is no repeat of Monday's eleven-basis-point intraday move in the ten-year.

The London morning is the first window of the day with enough liquidity to convert an overnight sequence of lower lows into a genuinely persistent path, so Tail firms to 23% and the mode is modelled as trend-down. This is a conditional reading and nothing about European structure has been observed at the assessment cutoff. The reference level into the session is the 30,409.25 overnight low. Crude holding above $93 on WTI and near $106.81 on Brent keeps the energy-to-inflation-to-yields channel open, which is why Stress firms to 79% while Tail stays five points short of the threshold that would change the mapped policy state.
